body:
The gated re-entry of the viola open chunk: it changed no code, no test, no dependency, no schema and no master text; it read and cleared the gated block on the live R2 reading.
R2, the live reading of viola open on the operator host, ran green: the new terminal window was placed on the parent window's workspace with the agent claude, and the wrapper recorded that window's address against the terminal's pid.
The reading ran with the desktop locked, on the operator's later word, so the block's wording that R2 runs on an unlocked host is disproved as a description; that wording lives only on the route and the ledger, not in any master.
It measured that the code at HEAD changed nothing R2 rests on in behaviour: the closed terminal argv with no shell, the bounded live wait, the wrapper's window step and the recorded window line are as R2 read them.
The ledger item for viola open's gated half moves from planned to implemented; no count or bound in any row moved.
The rule that viola open's live wait is bounded at 30 s: R2 read it holding on a real host and the session confirms the wait's behaviour unchanged; the bound value itself did not move.
The rule that the wrapper's window step waits at most 5 s for the terminal's window: R2 read the window found and recorded within it; the value did not move.
The rule that each compositor read is bounded at 5 s: the window step and the live wait read the compositor under it during R2; unchanged.

The rule that live readings never gate: R2 is a live reading that cleared a gated ledger block, a hand-fired operator reading, not a CI gate; a picker should check the row still holds that a live reading never fails the build.
The TUI screen-reader target of Orca with foot on Hyprland: R2 opened a foot window on Hyprland beside the parent, the same terminal and compositor the target names; no screen-reader pass was run.
The rules that time bounds fall on the driver only and never on the human: the bounded waits R2 exercised are the driver's, and the session adds no time limit on the user.
The decision that the tui terminal belongs to the child and zero viola bytes reach the terminal: viola open spawns the terminal with a closed argv and no shell, unchanged, and writes nothing to it.
The manual-checks-are-supplemental rules: R2 is a manual operator reading recorded as evidence and gates no CI build.
CLI refusal, fault and hint layout rows, exit codes and their --json documents: no refusal, code word, hint or exit code was added or changed.
The viola list board, caption, colour, SGR and NAME truncation rows: no output line or colour rule moved.
The TUI passthrough contract rows for human keystrokes, focus, mouse and resize sequences, vendor content and the vt100 feed panic: the passthrough was not touched.
The CI integration, a11y tool choice, mutation audit and SLO budget rows: no gate, workflow, threshold or suite changed; the deferred whole-suite runs belong to the light gate, not to a change.
viola up, viola revive, viola link, viola wait and viola verify output contracts: none of those verbs changed in this session.
The absence rows for a web or graphical frontend, touch surface, rendered page and internationalization: no such capability was added.

The gated half of viola open (ledger row v2-07) was cleared: the live R2 reading on the operator's Hyprland host read green, the new terminal window placed on the parent window's workspace with the agent claude, and its recorded address found by the terminal's pid.
No source, test, config or spec text changed in this gated run; no code, dependency, schema, harness or gate surface moved, and nothing was retired.
The code at HEAD was diffed against the code R2 read and nothing R2's reading rests on changed in behaviour: the closed terminal argv with no shell, the bounded live wait, the wrapper's window step and the window record in the snapshot replay and the board.
A measurement disproved the gated block's wording that R2 runs at an unlocked desktop: R2 ran with the desktop locked, after a green no-start probe, on the operator's later grant.
The operator's relayed answers make a set of PROVISIONAL rows his: among them the recorded cwd on up's terminal argv and the instance snapshot's cwd; rows resting only on a delegate's technical word stay PROVISIONAL for the epoch batch.
The instance snapshot contract item cwd: its PROVISIONAL state is discharged by the operator's own answer (the recorded cwd handed on up's terminal argv, as built), no change to what it says.
The decision that window features target Hyprland: now backed by a green live reading on the operator's Hyprland host (the window placed on the parent window's workspace), no change to what it says.

The decision that hyprctl and the terminal are spawned directly with a closed argv and no shell: the reading confirmed it unchanged at HEAD; any row whose state waits on the live R2 reading may move off provisional.

The CLI verb open and its name, and the viola open exit codes 0, 1 and 2: the verb's gated half is now met; a row whose state or note says the open verb is gated on R2 or pending its live reading is stale.

The window record: the instance snapshot item window, the event kind window, its event data and the wrapper's window event append, recorded by the wrapper from the terminal's pid; confirmed by the reading, unchanged.
The process-exit detail values terminal-not-found and window-not-found and the bounded live wait they end: unchanged and pinned, a row noting them unproven on a live host is stale.

The decision that the spawn directory is confined to the snapshot and the decision that the run reads its pair from the record: a row PROVISIONAL on the operator's fork over the recorded cwd is his now.

The Hyprland seam error contract items (malformed, oversize, refused, unreachable, unsupported) and the decision that viola-hyprland is the one compositor seam: the live reading went through this seam green, unchanged.
Any row that states the open placement must be read at an unlocked desktop or names the host's lock state as a precondition: the reading ran under a locked desktop, so such wording is disproved.
The board read model and the decision that list reads state without a wrapper, as far as they carry the window item: confirmed unchanged by the reading's diff check.
The send, wait, last, answer, pause, release, link and unlink paths, the wheel, dialogs, hooks and the channel frame contracts: the session touched no part of them.
The MCP server, its tools and their results: not reached.
The capability ledger of CLI behaviour, its stamps and viola verify: the v2-07 flip is a route ledger state, not a CLI capability ledger row.
The build system, CI/CD, dependency policy, toolchain pin, lint and coverage floors: no gate, threshold or floor moved.
The revive, up selection and up ordering rules and the focus verb: unchanged by this gated run.
Occupied names of binaries, crates, environment variables and test seams: none taken or freed.
The design philosophy, project intent and the absence rows (daemon, graphical frontend, database, hosting, network port): not reached.

This session is the gated wrap of the viola open chunk. Its gated implement changed no file of the tree, no symbol, no schema and no dependency.
It measured the gated half of viola open on the live host: the R2 reading came back green as placement=placed workspace=1 parent_workspace=1 agent=claude. The terminal window opened on its parent window's workspace, and the wrapper recorded the window it found by the terminal's pid.
The ledger item v2-07 (viola open) moves from planned to implemented and is now cleared. No count or qualifier in any master moved.
It disproved one claim. The gated block said the reading would run at the operator host, unlocked. In fact R2 ran with the desktop locked, after a green no-start probe, because the operator later granted it that way. That wording belongs to the route and the ledger, and no design-system row states it.
The operator's relayed answers discharge PROVISIONAL rows only on his own forks. These include the recorded cwd on viola up's terminal argv, which he affirmed as built. Rows that are PROVISIONAL on a delegate's technical word stay PROVISIONAL. The R2 carry and the a11y time-bound carry are both spent.

The open command name (name/command/open) now has its gated live proof read green. Any cell on it that marks the verb as gated, pending a live reading or PROVISIONAL on the operator's R2 answer is now stale.

The placement word placed (contract/placement-word/placed) has now been measured on a live host. R2's green line reads placement=placed with workspace equal to parent_workspace, which is the window beside its parent.

The other placement words (contract/placement-word/*) belong to the same placement outcome that R2 exercised live. Any of them still PROVISIONAL on the operator's R2 fork is discharged. Those resting on a delegate's technical word stay PROVISIONAL.
The origin word agent (contract/origin-word/agent) is the origin recorded by the wrapper in R2's green line (agent=claude). It is confirmed on a live run.

Indirect, through the window the wrapper records: the window rule and the board item that carry a window were pinned unchanged against what R2 read. Rows over the board's window field (viola list board, the list table) are confirmed, not changed.

The viola up terminal argv carrying the recorded cwd (contract/cli-verb-output/up, viola up output, viola up outcome words) is now the operator's own answer (U2b, as built). Any design-system row PROVISIONAL on that fork is discharged.
The a11y time-bound rows landed at the viola up wrap had a carry that is now spent. Any design-system row whose cell still names that carry or a time bound owed to this wrap goes stale.

Any row conditioning the live window proof on an unlocked desktop is contradicted by the measurement, because R2 ran with the desktop locked. The sweep found no design-system row stating this. A picker should flag only a row whose cell actually says so.

The viola focus exit-1 codes (contract/viola-focus-exit-1-codes/*) share the placement vocabulary with open. A cell that ties their proof to R2 still being unread is stale, because R2 now reads green.
Brand identity: the strip, readback-box, phraseology and expression-level decisions are not reached. No output form or wording changed.
Color palette, typography, spacing, depth, border radius and iconography are not reached. No glyph, column, colour token or SGR rule moved.
CLI exit codes, exit-21 causes, refusal hints, strict-modes refusals, catch sites and wrapper fault details are not reached. No refusal or exit path changed.
The revive, verify, send, wait, last, link and unlink output contracts and their refusal lists are not reached.
The web surface absence, the rendered-page absence and the CLI tape absence are not reached. No capability was added or removed.
Anti-patterns and the self-validation protocol (swap, squint, readback-box signature checks) are not reached.
The version-gate stamps decision that says unlocked and capped only shares the word unlocked. It concerns a file read with no lock, not the desktop, and it stays true.

This session is the gated half of viola open: it changed no code, no symbol, no schema, no dependency and no spec text.
It measured the operator-host reading R2: a terminal window opened by viola open was placed, its workspace the parent window's workspace, the agent claude, the wrapper recording the window found by the terminal's pid.
The reading ran on a locked desktop under the operator's own grant, not unlocked as the gated block first worded it; that wording lives on the ledger and route line, in no master row.
It confirmed the code at HEAD changed nothing R2 rests on: the closed argv of one element each, the bounded live wait, the wrapper's window step and the recorded window line are as R2 read them.
The ledger entry v2-07 moves from planned to implemented; no count or qualifier any row holds moved.

The viola open verb contract (a terminal window per session beside its parent, closed allowlist, no shell, window and origin recorded by the wrapper): its operator-host gate is now met green; the contract text stands, only its proof moved from pending to read.
The viola open --parent default contract: the reading placed the new window on the parent window's workspace, confirming the default as written; no wording changes.
Any row that marks viola open's window placement or its terminal spawn as gated, pending or unproven on the operator host is now stale: the gated reading is green.
Any row in a PROVISIONAL state on an operator fork for viola open is discharged by the operator's relayed answers; rows provisional only on a delegate's technical word stay provisional.
Indirect: the revive window-placement contract sits beside open's placement; it is touched only where it cites open's placement as unproven or gated.
The board, list, BAY line, readback mirror and send output rows: no rendering, column, width or wording changed.
The CLI exit codes, refusal line form, hints and --json error detail rows: no code, cause or hint was added or moved.
The run, revive, send, wait, last, verify, plugin install, link, wheel and mcp verb contracts: none of their behaviour changed.
The token rendering rows and the styling, banner, spinner, pager and progress decisions: untouched.
The viola up and viola focus verb contracts: their chunks are separate; this session moved nothing of them.
The web surface absence and the deep-links absence: no surface was added.

This session is the gated wrap of the viola open chunk. It changed no product code, no config, no dependency and no master text.
It measured one thing, the R2 live reading, and the reading came back green. viola open's terminal window was placed on its parent window's workspace, and the wrapper recorded the window address by the terminal's pid.
The reading ran on a locked desktop after a green probe that started nothing. The operator granted this run on a locked desktop. The block's wording, at the operator host unlocked, did not match how R2 ran.
Ledger item v2-07 flips from planned to implemented. No count or qualifier that a master row holds moved. The diff between the commit R2 read and the head changed no behaviour that R2 rests on.
The operator's relayed answers settle the provisional rows that sit on his own forks, including the recorded cwd being kept to the snapshot. Rows that are provisional only on a delegate's technical word stay provisional.
decision/open-closed-argument-allowlist: the R2 reading confirms that viola open's terminal is spawned with the closed argv, one element each. The rule is unchanged.
decision/open-terminal-direct-spawn: the reading confirms that viola open spawns its terminal directly, with no shell. The rule is unchanged.

decision/window-step-moves-own-terminal-window and decision/hyprland-recorder-moves-own-window: R2 placed only the session's own terminal window, on the parent's workspace. Both rules are confirmed live.

decision/window-origin-authenticates-nothing and decision/window-record-kept-to-snapshot-and-event-log: the wrapper recorded the window address and its origin in the snapshot and in clients. Both rules are confirmed, not changed.

decision/open-ancestor-walk-in-memory and decision/board-window-and-origin-re-parsed: these rules cover viola open's ancestry walk and the board's window item. The report says neither behaviour changed between the commit R2 read and the head.
decision/cwd-only-in-snapshot and decision/spawn-cwd-snapshot-only: the operator's relayed answer, Yes as built, makes these his. Any provisional state they hold on his fork is discharged.

Live-rig rows that are provisional on a delegate's technical word (the live-rig decisions in secret-management and data-protection): they stay provisional for the epoch batch. The operator's answers do not discharge them.
decision/run-window-flags-checked and decision/hyprctl-read-deadline: these rules cover the wrapper's window step and the hyprctl read. R2 exercised both rules live, and both are unchanged.
decision/version-gate-strict-stamps-read: its word unlocked means a stamps read without a file lock. It has nothing to do with the desktop lock state of R2.
Dependency-security rows (pins, cargo-deny, advisory floors, toolchains): no dependency or tool version moved.
Channel, MCP, hook, send, answer and revive contracts and their refusal codes: no protocol surface or error code changed.
Strict-modes, socket-directory and peer-euid checks: no check order or refusal changed.
Secret-management, CI canary-scan and workflow rows: no workflow, secret or upload changed.
Absences (network, hosting, accounts, database, release stage): no capability was added or removed.

This is the gated re-entry of the viola open chunk: it changed no file of the product, its tests, scripts or config, and it added, renamed and retired nothing.
It cleared the chunk's gated block on the live reading R2, already fired and read green: viola open placed a terminal window beside its parent, workspace 1 on parent workspace 1, the wrapper recorded the window address, agent claude.
Ledger item v2-07 moves from planned to implemented. No count or qualifier in any master moved.
Measured: the gated block assumed an unlocked desktop at the operator host. R2 actually ran with the desktop locked, after a green no-start probe, because the operator granted that. The block cleared on his grant, not on its original wording.
The code R2 read and the code at HEAD differ in nothing R2's reading rests on: the closed terminal argv, the live wait, the wrapper's window step and the snapshot window record are unchanged in behaviour.
The whole unit, integration and e2e harness runs were held on the operator's word and passed to the wrap's light gate. The operator's answers discharge only the PROVISIONAL rows on his own forks. Rows that rest on a delegate's technical word stay PROVISIONAL.
The decision that real window placement is proven only live. Its gated live reading R2 is now read green, so any cell that holds R2 as pending, owed or planned is stale.

The decision that a live reading is recorded as a reading, never as verification. The R2 reading clears a gated block and flips a ledger state, and the rule over how that reading is recorded applies to it.
Any row that states the gated live reading's precondition as an unlocked desktop at the operator host. R2 ran with the desktop locked, after a green no-start probe, on the operator's grant.
The decision that the real window raise is proven only by the gated live reading R3. It names R2 as its neighbour, and R2 is now read green. The claim stands true but its reference moved state.
The decision that the live rig runs clean of the firing session. It stays PROVISIONAL on a delegate's technical word and is not discharged by the operator's answers.

The decisions against human-in-loop verification and manual smoke steps. The R2 gated reading is an operator-granted live firing that clears a gated block, and these rules govern whether such a reading counts as a gate.
The decision that quality gates are never skipped. In the gated run the whole unit, integration and e2e harness runs were held unrun on the operator's word and handed to the wrap's light gate.
The fake foot stand-in's spawn record and the shared teardown of a stand-in terminal's tree. These are the test doubles behind the viola open cases whose behaviour the session confirmed unchanged.
CI integration, actions pinning, workflow permissions, cargo-deny, the advisory scans and the toolchain pins. No workflow, dependency or toolchain changed.
Coverage floors, mutation gate thresholds, perf budgets and hook deadlines. No threshold, floor or bound moved.
The send, answer, wait, release, revive and MCP tool contracts, the wrapper channel and JSON-RPC errors, and the exit codes. No product surface changed.
Fixtures, the fake agent's command line and receipts, recorded hook payloads and the hygiene walks. No fixture was recorded or edited.
The test harness contract: boot, cleanup, status, the gate, pre-push, secret scan, session records and the log format. No harness code or document shape changed.
The real fleet re-open proven by R4 and the viola up rows. These belong to another chunk's gated reading, not to this session.
